title: microfeature-portfolio-scratch
content:
Goal: collect a compact set of small, independently deployable microfeatures that move unit economics or latency in measurable ways, and stage them as a portfolio of experiments (A/B or canary) with low rollout friction.

Notes to self:
- keep each item small (<= 2-week eng work) so we can iterate and measure quickly
- prioritize features that are reversible (toggleable at proxy or runtime)
- include a lightweight telemetry plan for every item (key metrics + expected delta)
- aim for 6–8 items to run across next quarter as a portfolio (diversify wins/risk)

Hypotheses (rough):
1) small prefix-caching for common system prompts will reduce tail latency by ~10% on hosted small-seq workloads
2) per-customer default fidelity tiers (auto downgrade on idle sessions) reduces token cost by 6–12% for <5% UX regressions
3) microbatching on low-concurrency customers (short windows) gives 8–15% cost improvement with negligible latency impact if window <= 75ms

Candidate microfeatures (ranked for experiment readiness):
A. Runtime toggle: system-prefix prefetch cache
  - idea: detect and cache first N kv entries for templates / system prompts per model-variant
  - dev estimate: 6d (impl + smoke + dashboarding)
  - telemetry: p50/p95 token-gen latency, cache hit ratio, error rate
  - quick roll: enable for 10% of traffic (low QPS customers)

B. Per-customer fidelity defaults (tiered by usage)
  - idea: add customer-level config that maps to model variants / sampling params (e.g., temp / top-p / model-size)
  - dev estimate: 8d (api change + console + migration script)
  - telemetry: average tokens per request, cost per request, user observable quality metric (mini-eval)
  - risk: product confusion; need clear naming + migration UI

C. Microbatching-with-window (adaptive windowing)
  - idea: batch short requests up to X ms for low-priority lanes; dynamically disable on latency spikes
  - dev estimate: 10d (serving runtime + experiment flag)
  - telemetry: batch size distribution, per-token cost, latency SLO violation rate

D. Token-level hint compression (heuristic)
  - idea: run cheap tokenization rules to collapse/normalize long repeated contexts (emails, logs) before send to model
  - dev estimate: 7d (lib + safety checks)
  - telemetry: reduction in input length, delta in output relevance score (automated eval), false-positive rate on compression

E. Cheap fallback model for non-critical routes (micro model routing)
  - idea: route routes flagged as low-importance to a smaller quantized variant with strict fallback to full model on low-confidence
  - dev estimate: 12d (routing policy + confidence signal)
  - telemetry: error/retry rate, cost delta, user satisfaction proxy

F. Tiny token-budgeting guardrail for assistant turn length
  - idea: per-turn max token budgets derived from conversation signals; enforce soft alerts + hard truncation only if budget exhausted
  - dev estimate: 4d
  - telemetry: avg tokens per turn, budget hits, downstream satisfaction metric if available

Experiment design template (for each microfeature):
- experiment id: feature-yy-mm-<short>
- audience: percent of traffic / specific customer cohort / internal-only
- duration: min 2 weeks + warmup where applicable
- primary metric: single metric with direction (cost per 1k tokens down, or p95 latency down, etc.)
- guardrail metrics: error rate, p99 latency, relevant quality eval (mini-eval or golden set)
- rollback criteria: >5% increase in error rate OR >2x expected latency regression OR negative quality delta beyond threshold

Quick measurement primitives I want instrumented before we start:
- per-request token cost and model variant used (already mostly available, need finer tags)
- per-turn micro-eval hooks: send small golden set with determinism to track quality drift per experiment cohort
- cohort assignment id surfaced in observability traces

Dependencies / blockers:
- small infra work to add runtime toggles to route decisions (SRE + runtime)
- console surface for customer opting and visibility (product + dx)
- lightweight mini-eval harness for rapid signal (research/applied-ml)

Potential fast experiments (can run with minimal infra):
- A/B prefix caching via client-side emulation (no runtime change) — simulate cache hits and measure with synthetic traces
- Per-customer default via config file for a handful of internal test customers
- Manual routing pilot for cheap fallback using existing feature-flagged route logic

Open questions / TODOs:
- what is acceptable product surface to communicate these toggles to customers? (console vs. API flag)
- need a default naming convention for tiers and variants to avoid confusion (proposal: \"economy\", \"standard\", \"high-fidelity\")
- who is the owner for mini-eval harness? tag: research/applied-ml or product-analytics?

Next actions (this week):
- pick top 3 candidates (A/B/C) and write short experiment briefs (owner + telemetry plan) — Marcus (me) to draft
- sync with SRE on runtime toggle feasibility Wed
- loop in Talia on console MVP for a simple toggle page
- quick spike: implement budget guardrail (F) in a feature-flagged branch to demo at next team sync

Notes: keep doc lightweight and treat as an active parking lot. Move items out to full PRD only when an experiment shows promising signal.

Reference links:
- early thread: slack #prod-econ -> convo thread ts=170923 (I'll paste link later)
- rough cost sims: spreadsheet (internal) -> will link when cleaned up

Personal comments: want experiments that are reversible and that give us clear dollar/unit impact. Avoid big single-shot migrations unless payoff > 30% unit improvement.
